## How Everything Fits Together

Here is the full chain from import to runtime, as confirmed by the source files:

```

  └── re-exports CORSMiddleware from starlette.middleware.cors

  └── .add_middleware() registers it into the middleware stack at app startup
```

### What each `add_middleware` parameter does

| Parameter | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `allow_origins` | `["http://localhost:3000", "http://localhost:5173"]` | **Explicit allowlist.** Only these two origins can make cross-origin requests. |
| `allow_credentials` | `True` | Allows cookies and `Authorization` headers to be sent cross-origin. |
| `allow_methods` | `["*"]` | All HTTP methods (`GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `DELETE`, `PATCH`, etc.) are permitted. |
| `allow_headers` | `["*"]` | All request headers (e.g. `Content-Type`, `Authorization`) are permitted. |

### ⚠️ One critical rule (enforced by the Starlette CORS spec)
> **`allow_origins` cannot be `["*"]` when `allow_credentials=True`.**

As confirmed by the multilingual docs in this repo (`docs/zh/`, `docs/ja/`, `docs/de/`, etc.), using a wildcard origin with credentials is forbidden by the browser CORS spec. By listing origins **explicitly** — exactly as done above — this constraint is correctly satisfied.
